translation: `Target` is defined as the proposition that there does not exist a finite-node state machine `N` (a value of `S1 Bool Bool`) simultaneously satisfying three conditions. Here a value `N : S1 Bool Bool` consists of: a finite type `N.A1` of nodes; for each node `n : N.A1`, a state type `N.A3 n`; an initial global state `N.a4` assigning an element of `N.A3 n` to every `n : N.A1`; a synchronous update function `N.a5` giving, for each node `n`, global state `σ : (m : N.A1) → N.A3 m`, and input `x : Bool`, a next state `N.a5 n σ x : N.A3 n`; and an output function `N.a6` mapping any global state to `Bool`. The three conditions on `N` inside the negated existential are: (1) `N.D12`: for all nodes `m` and `n` in `N.A1` with `m ≠ n`, it is not the case that there exist both a non-empty directed chain (one or more steps) from `m` to `n` and a non-empty directed chain from `n` to `m` in the dependency relation `N.D8`, where `N.D8 a b` holds iff there exist two global states `σ, σ'` agreeing at every node `k ≠ a` and an input `x : Bool` such that `N.a5 b σ x ≠ N.a5 b σ' x` (thus mutual reachability between distinct nodes is forbidden, whereas self-dependencies with `m = n` are not forbidden). (2) `N.D25 3`: for every node `n : N.A1`, its state type `N.A3 n` is finite and has cardinality at most `3` (`Nat.card (N.A3 n) ≤ 3`, so `3` states per node are allowed). (3) `S1.D6 N (d26 3)`: for every finite sequence `xs : List Bool`, the Boolean output of `N` on `xs`—obtained by starting from `N.a4`, folding the synchronous update `fun σ x => fun n => N.a5 n σ x` left to right over `xs`, and applying `N.a6`—equals the output of `d26 3` on `xs`. Here `d26 3` is the single-node (`A1 = Unit`) machine with state type `Fin 3`, initial state `0`, update rule adding `1` modulo `3` on input `true` and leaving the state unchanged on input `false`, and output `true` iff the final state is `0` (i.e., iff the number of `true` entries in `xs` is divisible by `3`). As written, `d26 3` itself satisfies all three conditions (vacuously satisfying `D12` since it has only one node, having `Nat.card (Fin 3) = 3 ≤ 3` for `D25 3`, and matching itself for `D6`), so the proposition `Target` is false.

divergences.description: The author's description states that each unit has 'at most two states per unit', whereas TARGET writes `N.D25 3`, allowing at most three states per unit (`Nat.card (N.A3 n) ≤ 3`). Because this bound appears inside a negated existential (`¬ ∃ N, ...`), changing `2` to `3` strictly strengthens the claim and makes `Target` false, as `d26 3` itself is a single-unit network satisfying `D12`, `D25 3`, and `S1.D6 (d26 3) (d26 3)`.

The description says 'a network, of any size' without explicitly restricting to finitely many units, whereas `S1` requires `Fintype A1` (any finite number of units), and fixes a specific synchronous Moore-machine interface with Boolean inputs and Boolean output testing whether the count of `true` inputs is `0` mod `3`.

judgement.summary: The description accurately reports what the passages say, but TARGET diverges materially from the author's description by writing `N.D25 3` (at most three states per unit) instead of `N.D25 2` (at most two states per unit). This wrong constant turns the intended impossibility claim into a false proposition trivially refuted by `d26 3` itself.
